_comment: The registry scripts/lineage.mjs enforces. Read its header first.
Every file that exists in more than one project must appear here, in exactly
one of the two lists. 'shared' files must be byte-identical everywhere they
appear; 'forks' are allowed to differ and must say why. A duplicated file in
neither list fails the gate, which is the point: it forces the question
'is this supposed to be the same file?' to be answered once, in writing,
instead of being discovered as a bug months later.

shared.why: The piggyback itself. Every project wraps window.fetch the same way; if this file ever differs between them, the thing the repository is teaching has forked.

The shapes crossing the postMessage boundary, mirroring the API response — schemas parsed at the boundary, with the TypeScript types inferred from them rather than written twice. A project that needed fewer fields would still receive them, so trimming buys nothing and costs the identity.
API response to a flat row shape. Pure, and identical in every project.
The feature as a pure function. This is the file a reader is most likely to copy out; it must be the same file in every project that has it.
Fixtures. Divergence here would make two projects' specs incomparable.
Pins the ordering and connector rules for the shared src/family/tree.ts.
Pins the shared src/family/rows.ts.

Pins the shared src/inject.ts: generation stamping, the getter that survives reassignment, and adopting a later wrapper without cycling. Every property in it fails silently in a browser, so it has to be the same spec wherever the file is.
Same test policy everywhere, including allowOnly: false.
One build script for every project, now that the per-project part — the entry-point list — lives in esbuild.config.mjs. It was a fork while it held both.

Every URL this extension builds, in one file. A project that built its own would be the project whose requests are not the ones the others were reviewed for — and the forward/reverse history distinction here is exactly the sort of detail that drifts silently once copied.

Pure template expansion, including the rule that an expansion which is not an absolute http(s) URL is not opened, plus the schema for one stored template — this is the shape each project's settings.ts salvages the stored link list against, entry by entry. Identical wherever the feature exists.

The only place in either project that writes an <a> the user can click, and the one render module called from TWO pages — the workflow list through syncDeepLinks(), a single workflow's own page through syncLinkAnchors(). Every anchor in the repository therefore carries the same three hardening attributes (target, rel=noopener noreferrer, referrerPolicy=no-referrer) and reports an unopenable URL the same way. A stage-local copy would let one page's links lose one of those attributes while the other kept it, which is the kind of difference nobody sees by eye.

The 'Last event' column and the retry badge. Byte-identical on purpose even though 03 draws a third control in the same cell: this file reads answers out of RenderOptions.info and never learns where they came from, so nothing about a later stage gives it a reason to differ. Two properties in it fail silently and must be proved once rather than twice — the column stays RECTANGULAR (every row gets exactly one cell, or the headers sit one column out from their data), and it is idempotent about POSITION as well as text, because moving a node that is already in place wakes the MutationObserver that called it.

The pure folds behind the links on a single workflow's page, including which activity an id found on the page resolves to. It reads responses the page fetched for itself and touches neither credentials nor the ledger, so nothing about a later stage gives it a reason to differ.
Where the detail-page links are allowed to sit in the UI's own layout, and how an id read off the page becomes one activity. Same file, same decision.
The seam that hands the page's own history and describe responses to the detail-page links. Deliberately separate from the request path, and the same in every project that has it.

The message shapes for the per-row questions, as schemas that validate them to the leaves and as the types inferred from those schemas — one declaration, so the wire and the compiler cannot drift apart. Both sides of a postMessage boundary read this file; a fork would be a protocol fork.

The isolated-world half of the per-row questions: batching, the cache, and the correlation check on the answer. 03 adds a second client of the same pattern (src/payloads/tooltip.ts) rather than changing this one.

The GENERIC pacing machinery, with the clock and the sleep injected — which is why it can be identical while its INSTANCE is not. 02 keeps that instance inline in the one file that issues requests; 03 moves it to src/page/requestPacing.ts because a second feature issues them too. The testable part must not fork, or the two projects' concurrency arguments become incomparable.
Pins the shared src/page/temporalApi.ts.
Pins the shared src/links/deepLink.ts, including every template that must NOT be opened.
Pins the shared src/detail/detail.ts.
Pins the shared src/detail/detailLinks.ts — both anchors, the idempotency of a second pass, and the fact that an unresolvable id gets no link at all.

Pins the shared src/rowInfo/rowInfo.ts schemas — the truth table for what crosses the message boundary, which is the file both worlds trust. It asserts the constraints this protocol adds and not the schema library's own primitive semantics, which is the rule every schema spec in the repository follows.
Pins the shared src/rowInfo/rowInfoClient.ts.

Pins withActivityScope, which is identical in both projects even though the rest of settings.ts is not: it is the fix for a stored links array that predates the activity template and therefore silently makes every per-activity link unreachable. The spec deliberately touches nothing else in settings.ts, so it can stay byte-identical across the two.

Pins the shared src/types.ts boundary schemas: the workflow-list envelope, the partial execution shape the row fold reads, and the message the page world posts. Byte-identical because the schemas are, and because the one property it exists to prove is a property of the composition rather than of any project — a malformed entry costs one row and never the whole list. It asserts no primitive semantics of the schema library itself; that rule is stated in its own header.

Pins the shared src/page/pacer.ts with a fake clock and no network: a slot held across a backoff, the longest overlapping Retry-After winning, and a success during a block not resetting the doubling. None of those is observable from a feature test, in either project.

Pins the deep-link buttons on the workflow LIST, over the shared src/links/deepLink.ts expansion. Half of it is about a URL that must NOT be clickable, including the case that only a re-render can produce: an anchor has to LOSE an href it was already given when the template is edited into something unsafe. 02 and 03 draw these buttons from the same code path, so the spec is byte-identical.

Pins the two columns that cost a request — the “Last event” cell and the retrying-activity badge — including the four different meanings an empty cell can have, the refresh control's cooldown, and the fact that a render pass must never act as though the control were pressed. 02 introduces both features and 03 changes neither, so the spec is byte-identical; its one forward-looking note is worded to be true in both stages.

forks.why: Each project's README opens with its own security card, in a fixed shape so the projects can be compared line by line. A shared README could not say '01 asks for no permissions and originates no request' and '02 asks for storage and DOES originate requests' at the same time, and that contrast is the repository's argument.

Each project's icon carries its own number and hue, both derived from its directory name by scripts/make-icons.mjs — several extensions loaded at once in a 16px toolbar have to be distinguishable, and one shared glyph makes hovering each in turn the only way to tell them apart. The reviewable artefact is still the script, not the PNG.
See icon-16.png.
See icon-16.png.
See icon-16.png.

01 has no deep links and no on/off switch, so its applyToTable takes no options object at all: applyToTable(tbody, lookup), and it still holds the class names and the tree prefix in the one file, because at that length there is nothing to find (wc -l 01-family-tree/src/render.ts). 02 and 03 pass RenderOptions, delegate to the render modules beside them, own restoreOriginalOrder and the master switch removeAllDecoration — which calls the former, because the row order is the one edit that leaves no node behind to sweep, and state the left-to-right order of the controls that share the workflow-id cell rather than letting it fall out of which feature the user switched on first; 03 additionally calls payloads/payloadButton.ts and ranks a third control into that order. Parameterising one file to cover both would put the settings vocabulary back into the project whose whole claim is that it has none.

The root class of everything the extension draws, plus the shape of one render pass. removeAllDecoration() can only be as honest as this list, so anything the master switch has to reach is named here; a node that only exists inside one of those roots stays with the file that draws it. REMOVABLE_ROOT_CLASSES is that list as a value, and render.ts builds its sweep selector from it. Forked because the ladder IS the difference: 03 adds PAYLOAD_CLASS and PANEL_CLASS to both the names and that list, and PANEL_CLASS names the only node in this repository that can hold decoded payload text, which is why the master switch has to take it away. Its RenderOptions carries the matching payloadsEnabled. Sharing one file would mean 02 declaring names for nodes it never draws, and a reviewer reading this file for '02 can show me a payload' would find the vocabulary for it. 01 has no copy: its class names are still in src/render.ts.
01's wiring uses no chrome.* API whatsoever — that is what lets its manifest omit permissions. 02 and 03 load settings, subscribe to changes and answer the popup. The difference IS the lesson.

Follows src/render.ts, and holds only the table itself: finding it, reading a row out of it, drawing the tree into it, and the master switch that has to take every decoration away again — which is also the only spec that asserts src/decoration.ts's class list is complete. The per-feature blocks live beside it — renderLinks, renderRowInfo and 03's renderPayloadButton, matching the source modules of the same names — and the first two are byte-identical and declared shared. 01's copy drops visibleRows and removeAllDecoration, which are about features it has not got; 03's differs from 02's by the payloadsEnabled it hands the master-switch spec, and by not repeating the control-order block — 03 asserts that order in renderPayloadButton.spec.ts, beside the newest of the three controls, while 02's two are asserted here because 02's newest control is the retry badge and renderRowInfo.spec.ts is shared byte-identically with 03. The assertions every project keeps (idempotency, <tr> recycling, unknown rows) are deliberately duplicated verbatim so each proves them on its own code.

01 has no .tuis-link buttons, no .tuis-last-event / .tuis-col-head column, no .tuis-retry badge, no .tuis-linkbar row beside the page's own tabs and no html.tuis-off master switch, so it ships none of those rules; 03 adds the .tuis-payload button and the .tuis-panel* overlay on top of 02's. The .tuis-prefix and .tuis-seg-* connector rules are the same in all three.

The permission ladder, which is the repository's main argument: 01 declares no permissions and no action; 02 and 03 declare storage and a popup. Names and descriptions differ so three loaded projects are distinguishable in chrome://extensions.
Per-project name, description and dependency set. 01 does not depend on @types/chrome, because it uses no chrome API.
01 sets "types": [] — it needs no ambient type package at all, and the typechecker is where that claim is enforced. 02 and 03 set "types": ["chrome"].

Entry points differ: 01 builds inject + content; 02 and 03 also build the popup and src/apiInject.ts — a second MAIN-world bundle, which 01 has no use for because it never issues a request. Only this list differs; everything else about the build is identical, which is why esbuild.mjs moved to "shared" when the options came out of it.

The trust boundary, and the one file where a stage difference is a SECURITY difference. Both copies own the same ledger and the same fetchForListedRun(), the only route to the page's Authorization header. 03 adds a second exported fetch, fetchFromPageWorld(), for the codec call: a caller-chosen origin, carrying no credential of ours. The two must never converge — one chooses the origin and spends the bearer, the other takes the origin from a message and spends nothing — and keeping them in a declared fork is what makes that diff readable rather than a refactor nobody re-reviewed.

The list of messages this extension accepts from the page, which is the list a reviewer enumerates. 02 accepts one; 03 accepts two, and the second names an outbound host of its own. That count is the whole point of the file, so it cannot be shared.

Identical logic, different OWNER of the pacer. 02 builds the instance here, because this is the only file that issues requests and the concurrency argument is checkable by reading it. 03 imports it from src/page/requestPacing.ts, because the payload path issues them too and a second makePacer() call would have given the extension two independent caps of four while both files still looked correct. The diff between these two copies is that lesson.

One stored shape per project, and defaults are a decision each stage makes for itself. 03 adds the payload toggle plus the one field that names an outbound host, and its default is the empty string — the only setting in this repository that defaults to off for a reason other than cost. It deliberately stores NO credential switch beside that host: a `codecIncludeCredentials` was designed, built and then deleted, because the endpoint arrives over postMessage and a default of off protects only the honest path through the popup. Each stored shape is a schema, so the fork is also the reason the deleted field is unreachable rather than merely unread — a key absent from the schema is absent from the parsed object, and 02's copy cannot be handed a codec endpoint through storage at all.

Follows src/settings.ts, which is itself a fork: the field sets differ, so the spec that reads them back cannot be byte-identical. Each project asserts the same four readings over its own shape — a stored false is off and anything else is the shipped default, one unusable field does not discard the ones beside it, the link list is salvaged entry by entry, and the scope backfill stops at the migration marker — and then the one assertion only its stage can make. 03 pins that a `codecIncludeCredentials` still sitting in somebody's chrome.storage.sync is not in the object the loader returns; 02 pins that a stored codec endpoint is not either, because this build has no such setting. tests/unit/settings.spec.ts stays shared beside it: that one covers the pure withActivityScope and touches nothing stage-specific.
Follows public/popup.html. 03 binds the payload toggle, the codec endpoint field and the verdict line that says, before anything is hovered, whether the value in the box will be used at all.

The popup is where a user is told what leaves their machine, so it cannot be shared between a project where nothing does and one where something can. 03 adds the Payloads section and the Codec server section — including the sentence that there is no option to pass an access token, and the footer line that payload data leaves the browser only if a codec server is named.

The render fixtures the spec files within each project share: the family, the placement lookup over it, a RenderOptions with every feature off, and the helpers that give a table a <thead> and press the column's refresh control. Forked by ONE line — 03's OPTIONS carries payloadsEnabled and 02's RenderOptions has no such field, the same difference src/decoration.ts is forked for. Everything else is byte-identical on purpose, because the two projects' render assertions are meant to be comparable. 01 has no copy: its render specs are a single short file with one fixture block and nothing to share.

Follows src/apiInject.ts, and holds the trust boundary only: what has to be learned from the page, what may be fetched with it, and the survival of a window.fetch wrapper the page installs later. The per-row questions are in tests/unit/apiInjectRowInfo.spec.ts and the egress path in 03's tests/unit/apiInjectCodec.spec.ts, both over the shared tests/apiInjectHarness.ts. Forked by ONE test: 03 asks the ledger to refuse a payload hover as well as a row question, which is how 'one gate, not one per feature' is asserted for the second feature that reaches the network. 02 has no second feature to assert it with.

Follows src/rowInfo/rowInfoServe.ts: one question per running row, its answer, and the request counting that keeps the cost of those questions from being a claim in a comment. Forked by TWO lines, both of them real — the pacer's warning names what it paused, and 03 shares that pacer across the row questions and the payload hover, so it says 'pausing requests' where 02 says 'pausing row info'; and the section banner says which of the stage's features are piggybacks, which differs because 03 has one more. 01 has no copy: it makes no requests of its own at all.

The fake network the apiInject spec files share, plus the helper that imports the two MAIN-world scripts in the manifest's order and the install/teardown pair without which listeners accumulate across tests. Forked because 03's is a strict SUPERSET: the forward-history body a payload hover reads, the encrypted fixture that is the only thing a codec server is reached for, a decoding endpoint in the fake network, and the two extra Seen fields — the request BODY and `credentials` — that let a spec assert what left the browser rather than only where it went. Sharing it would mean 02 carrying fixtures for a feature it does not have. 01 has no copy.
